output.brief: The October night premium shortfall was caused by a pay rule change, not by your data. On 22 Oct an Ardentra consultant applied a standard template to night premium rule NSP-02. It was logged as a label correction with no effect on pay. The template also moved the premium start from 20:00 to 22:00. The platform's audit trail records this, and the parallel runs used 20:00. Internal audit's recalculation shows 147 of 158 night workers underpaid, each by exactly the premium for the 20:00–22:00 hours. The 11 correctly paid staff are rostered from 22:00. Re-running October with the window set back to 20:00 gave correct pay for all 158. Data quality, timesheets, the bank file and the release 7.4 software don't explain the pattern. I'm quite sure of this. Don't suspend the HR team or reload the data, and don't accept the clause 14.3 cost. Don't roll back release 7.4, because it carries the tax table needed for November. Have Ardentra restore the 20:00 window, verify it in the test tenant before 24 Nov, and make off-cycle payments to everyone underpaid. Also review how Ardentra's change entries are approved. The fall in night overtime cover may be partly caused by the pay shortfall and partly by the rota trial. The evidence can't separate the two, so don't pause the trial yet.
